title: Introduce token trajectory metrics and alert weighing
author: Elena Markov
description:
Motivation: long-tail production incidents are often driven by subtle changes in per-token behavior over the life of an invocation (e.g. warmup spikes, backend stalls during midstream, or finalization overheads). Existing token aggregates (total tokens, avg latency) miss shape-level regressions. This PR adds a lightweight "token trajectory" metric that summarizes per-token latency/cost as a normalized time series per invocation and exposes cohort-level summaries for alerting and dashboards.

What this change does: 1) Collect per-token delta samples in the serving runtime and emit a compact trajectory sketch per invocation (quantiles of normalized token index vs latency/cost). 2) Introduce token_trajectory_score and token_trajectory_cohort labels to group invocations by shape (e.g. front-loaded, mid-spike, tail-heavy). 3) Add an alert weighing/composer service that re-calibrates SLO alert thresholds based on cohort volatility and traffic weight to reduce noisy long-tail alerts. 4) Provide a Grafana dashboard (trellis view) and a small set of evals to catch regressions in trajectory shape.

Design notes: collection uses reservoir sampling + compact histogram to cap memory and network overhead. Trajectory sketches are emitted as additional metric series (prometheus remote write friendly) and as optional trace annotations when the invocation crosses a latency or cost threshold. The alert composer subscribes to cohort drift signals and calculates a weighted threshold multiplier per route/tenant; thresholds are bounded to avoid masking true outages.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime sampling and sketch plumbing (telemetry/metrics/token_trajectory.go)
- [x] Cohort classifier and stable hashing (observability/cohort/classifier.go)
- [x] Alert weighing/composer and integration tests (alerts/composer.go)
- [x] Grafana panels and saved dashboard JSON (dashboards/token-trajectory.jsonnet)
- [x] Unit + integration tests 
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout (feature_flags.enable_token_trajectory)

Backward compatibility: trajectory emission is opt-in behind a feature flag and defaults to off for tenants with strict quota. No breaking API changes.

Performance: local microbenchmarks show ~0.3% median throughput regression at 99th percentile concurrent serving with the default reservoir size. Memory overhead is capped per-worker (configurable).

Related: complements ENG-8421 (cohort-aware alerting), follows up on previous token shape telemetry work but focuses on per-invocation shape and alert weighting rather than aggregate rollups.
